required_outcomes: Tells the landlord that the tenant has fixed the toilet, so the plumber visit is not needed for the toilet, and that only the bedroom window needs attention.
Asks the landlord whether he will arrange someone suitable for the window (a plumber is not the right trade) or would like the agency to send one of its contractors.
Puts the case on hold or schedules a follow-up awaiting the landlord’s answer, with a review date.
acceptable_alternatives: Asking the landlord whether his plumber can also look at the window, provided the question about the window's trade is still raised.
Telling the tenant that the landlord had arranged a plumber for tomorrow morning and that the agency has told him only the window now needs doing, so she knows someone may still call.
positive_behaviours: Tells the tenant the landlord has been updated and that a reply is awaited, without inventing a visit time for the window.
Notes that the landlord's email was most likely written before he saw the tenant's update at event 006.
red_flags: Questioning which property the landlord means when his email names no other address.
prohibited_actions: Assigning an agency maintenance provider before the landlord has decided how the window is handled.
Telling the tenant that the window will be fixed tomorrow.
critical_failures: Recording the landlord's plumber visit as his decision on the window and closing the landlord-approval step without asking about the window.
